responses.sql: SELECT t.ordertypedist, COUNT(*) AS matched_records FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord t ON t.transreg = a.translink WHERE a.patsim >= 0.439 GROUP BY t.ordertypedist

assumptions.assumption: "High similarity" means patsim >= 0.439 (cutoff inclusive); the request does not say whether the cutoff itself is included.

Each matched (advancedbehavior, transactionrecord) pair counts as one matched record. Since transreg is the primary key, each advanced behaviour record matches at most one transaction record, so the pair count equals the number of matched advanced behaviour records.
Records with a NULL ordertypedist form their own group. GROUP BY puts NULLs in a single group, so no extra handling is needed.

alternatives.interpretation: High similarity means strictly greater than the cutoff (patsim > 0.439).
